property_summary: The onERC721Received function must return the selector ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector (0x150b7a02), but the buggy version returns bytes4(0xdeadbeef), breaking safe mint/transfer checks.

The onERC721Received function must return the magic value ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector (0x150b7a02); the mutant returns bytes4(0), so calling onERC721Received on the contract returns a different value.
For any input that does not revert, onERC721Received must return the selector ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector; the mutant returns the zero value for all inputs.

After initialization, the baseToken address stored in the contract must equal the _baseToken parameter supplied to initialize. The mutant forces baseToken to address(0), violating this equality for any non-zero _baseToken argument.
After initialization, the baseToken() getter must return the _baseToken address that was passed to initialize(); the mutant forces it to return address(0xdead) regardless.
After initialization, the baseToken state variable must equal the provided _baseToken argument; the buggy version leaves it as address(0) regardless.
After initialize is called, the nft() getter must return the address passed as _nft; the bug returns address(0) instead.
After initialization, the nft state variable must equal the address passed as the _nft parameter; the mutant leaves it at address(0).

After initialization, the nft address returned by the public getter nft() must equal the _nft argument passed to initialize; the bug sets nft to baseToken instead, so for any _nft != _baseToken the getter returns the wrong address.
After initialize is called, c.nft() must equal the _nft parameter passed to initialize; the bug sets nft to address(this) instead.
After initialization, the changeFee state variable must equal the _changeFee parameter passed to initialize. The buggy version drops this assignment, so changeFee stays zero regardless of the input.
After initialization, the contract's changeFee state variable must equal the _changeFee parameter supplied to initialize; the mutant hardcodes it to 1, breaking this rule.

After initialize, the stored feeRate MUST equal the _feeRate argument passed (unless it exceeded the cap of 5000, in which case the call reverts); the bug stores a constant 0 instead, violating equality for any non-zero admissible feeRate.
After initialize, feeRate must equal the passed _feeRate argument (reference) but the bug leaves it at zero regardless of the argument.
After initialize, feeRate must match _feeRate (reference) but the bug leaves it zero regardless of the argument.
After initialization, the stored feeRate must not exceed 5000; the buggy version allows a feeRate above 5000.
After initialization, feeRate must equal the supplied _feeRate; the mutant sets feeRate to _changeFee instead, so for any call where _feeRate != _changeFee the invariant fails.
After a successful call to initialize, the initialized state variable must be true; the mutant fails to set it, leaving initialized as false, which allows re-initialization.
After deployment, calling initialize should always revert on already-initialized contracts, but the mutant allows repeated initialization.
